key_terms.meaning: The order of an ODE is the highest derivative of the unknown function that appears in it.
The degree is the power of the highest derivative after the ODE is cleared of radicals and fractions in derivatives.
An ODE is linear when y and its derivatives appear only to the first power and are not multiplied together; first order form is y′ + P(x)y = Q(x).
A family of solutions containing as many arbitrary constants as the order of the ODE.
A solution obtained from the general solution by fixing the arbitrary constant or constants.
A solution not obtainable from the general solution by choosing the constant.
An equation that can be written dy/dx = g(x)h(y), so all y terms go with dy and all x terms with dx.
An equation of the form dy/dx = f(y/x); the ratio y/x controls the right side.
An equation M(x,y)dx + N(x,y)dy = 0 with ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x, so the left side is dF for some F(x,y).
A function μ(x) or μ(x,y) that multiplies a non-exact or non-linear equation and makes it exact or linear.
An equation y′ + P(x)y = Q(x); P and Q depend only on x.
An equation y′ + P(x)y = Q(x)yⁿ with n not 0 or 1; it reduces to linear by z = y^(1−n).
A substitution, such as z = y^(1−n) or z = log y, that turns a nonlinear first-order equation into a linear one.
An ODE together with a value y(x₀)=y₀ that the solution must satisfy.
|f(x,y₁) − f(x,y₂)| ≤ L|y₁ − y₂| for some constant L and all y₁,y₂ in the region.
The sequence y_{n+1}(x) = y₀ + ∫ from x₀ to x f(t,y_n(t)) dt used to build a solution.
If f(x,y) is continuous on a rectangle around (x₀,y₀), the IVP y′=f(x,y), y(x₀)=y₀ has a solution near x₀.
If f is continuous and Lipschitz in y on a rectangle, the IVP has exactly one solution near x₀.
dF = (∂F/∂x)dx + (∂F/∂y)dy; exact equations ask for M dx + N dy to equal such a dF.
F(x,y) whose partial derivatives are M and N; then the exact equation has solution F(x,y)=C.

takeaways: Classify first: order, degree and linearity tell you which later method can even apply.
Separable equations are solved by moving all y terms to one side and all x terms to the other, then integrating each side alone.
A homogeneous first-order equation depends on y/x, and v = y/x turns it into a separable equation in v and x.
An exact equation passes the test ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x and is solved by finding F(x,y)=C.
For y′ + P(x)y = Q(x), the integrating factor e^(∫P dx) turns the left side into the derivative of one product.
Bernoulli equations become linear after z = y^(1−n).
Continuity of f gives existence near x₀; continuity plus a Lipschitz condition in y gives uniqueness.
Picard iteration builds the solution as a limit of repeated integrations.
bank_note: Long answers usually reward method selection: classify first, state the exactness or Lipschitz condition, show the substitution or integrating factor, and finish with the general or particular solution.

bank.q: Define order, degree and linearity of a first-order ODE. Classify y′ + x y = x², (y′)² + y = 0 and y′ = y² + x.
outline: Order is the highest derivative present.
Degree is the power of the highest derivative after clearing radicals and fractions.
Linearity means y and y′ appear to the first power and not multiplied together.
y′ + x y = x² is first order, first degree, linear.
(y′)² + y = 0 is first order, second degree, nonlinear.
y′ = y² + x is first order, first degree, nonlinear.

bank.q: State the exactness criterion for M(x,y)dx + N(x,y)dy = 0 and explain why the solution is F(x,y)=C when the criterion holds.
outline: Explain that the left side becomes dF = M dx + N dy.
Integrate one partial derivative and match the other.
The constant C records the initial condition or family parameter.

bank.q: Explain why multiplying y′ + P(x)y = Q(x) by e^(∫P dx) makes the left side a single derivative.
outline: Compute μ′ = μP by the chain rule.

bank.q: State Picard–Lindelöf theorem for y′=f(x,y), y(x₀)=y₀, and explain the roles of continuity and the Lipschitz condition.
outline: Continuity of f on a rectangle gives existence near x₀.
Picard iteration y_{n+1}=y₀+∫f(t,y_n)dt builds the solution.
State the result on some interval around x₀.
Put y = vx, so y′ = v + x dv/dx.
Reduce to a separable equation in v and x.
Integrate and replace v by y/x.
Integrating factor μ = e^(∫2/x dx) = x².
Integrate to get x²y = x⁵/5 + C.

bank.q: Solve the Bernoulli equation y′ + y = x y².
outline: Solve the linear equation for z.
Return to y = 1/z and give the general solution.

bank.q: Use Picard iteration for y′ = x+y, y(0)=1 to find y₁ and y₂.
outline: y₂ = 1 + ∫ from 0 to x (t + y₁(t)) dt.

bank.q: For M dx + N dy = 0, derive an integrating factor μ(x) when (M_y − N_x)/N depends only on x, and use it on (x²+y²)dx + xy dy = 0.
outline: Multiply and solve the exact equation for F(x,y)=C.

bank.q: Classify y′ = (x²+y²)/(xy), choose a method, and solve it.
outline: Rewrite as y′ = x/y + y/x, so it is homogeneous.
Also note it is Bernoulli with n=−1.
Integrate to get the implicit solution.
Check that the chosen substitution is valid where xy ≠ 0.

bank.q: Discuss existence and uniqueness for y′ = √|y|, y(0)=0, and show that uniqueness fails.
outline: f(x,y)=√|y| is continuous near the origin.
It is not Lipschitz in y at y=0.
Show y=x²/4 for x≥0 is another solution through (0,0).

bank.q: Classify and solve y′ + P(x)y = Q(x)yⁿ, then explain how the case n=1 differs.
outline: For n not 0 or 1 it is Bernoulli.
Use z=y^(1−n) to reduce to linear form.
Solve the linear equation for z.
If n=1, the equation is already linear after moving the y term to the left.

glossary.def: An equation containing an unknown function of one variable and one or more of its derivatives.
The highest derivative present in the differential equation.
The power of the highest derivative after the equation is cleared of radicals and fractions in derivatives.
An ODE in which the unknown and its derivatives appear only to the first power and are not multiplied together.
An ODE that is not linear, for example because y or y′ appears squared or in a product.
A solution family containing arbitrary constants equal in number to the order of the ODE.
A single solution obtained by fixing the arbitrary constants in the general solution.
A solution that cannot be obtained from the general solution by any choice of constants.
A differential equation with a prescribed value of the solution at one point.
A first-order equation that can be written as dy/dx = g(x)h(y).
A function f with f(λx,λy)=λⁿf(x,y); in first-order equations this often means the right side depends only on y/x.
An expression M dx + N dy that equals dF for some function F.
A multiplier that changes an equation into an exact or linear equation.
An equation of the form y′ + P(x)y = Q(x).
An equation y′ + P(x)y = Q(x)yⁿ with n not 0 or 1.
A bound |f(x,y₁)−f(x,y₂)| ≤ L|y₁−y₂| that controls how fast f changes with y.
Repeated integration starting from y₀ to build a sequence of approximations to the IVP solution.
A theorem giving conditions under which an IVP has at least one solution.
A theorem giving conditions under which an IVP has at most one solution.
dF = F_x dx + F_y dy, the differential of a function F(x,y).
A function F(x,y) whose partial derivatives equal M and N in an exact equation.
The arbitrary constant produced by an indefinite integration; in an ODE it often becomes the parameter of the general solution.
